reasons: A's slogans have some real Russian play (батон/батут sound play, 'Один батон на район' rhyme and double meaning, спальный/просыпается contrast), though 'Просыпает' is misused (it means 'oversleeps') and the commentary has a grammar slip. B builds its jokes on an invented prison-slang idiom 'отбывать батон', and its explanations contain errors and nonsense ('анти-колоние', 'оркестр, рэли'), so it delivers almost no real wordplay. Several of B's slogans ('Никакого батона', 'Батон, который не бьёт') are confusing or would hurt a bakery sign.

A: 'Просыпает' means 'oversleeps', not 'wakes up', so slogan 4 says the opposite of the intended pun
B: 'Отбывать батон' is not an existing prison-slang expression; the explanation is fabricated
'анти-колоние' is not a correct Russian word form
The explanation of slogan 5 ('оркестр, рэли') is meaningless
